title: Phenotypic Adaptation and Redox Cycle Resonance in Low Oxygen Conditions
summary: This cluster of processes and phenotypes is centered around the effects of low oxygen conditions on cellular metabolism and genetic stability. Low DO/high respiration is associated with several processes, including the RNA-processing, RNA-modification, and sequencing-readout landscape, and the substitution-class-dependent response. Mismatch-rate and candidate variant-rate analyses have identified various genetic changes, including A > T, T > C/A > G, and collapsed C > T/G > A-compatible class, which are linked to the largest mismatch-rate increase and predominance. These findings suggest that low oxygen conditions lead to phenotypic adaptation and changes in the redox cycle resonance framework, affecting the redox-defined metabolic phases and transcriptome fidelity.
